section_summary: This section covers proceedings of and developments surrounding the Japanese Imperial Diet from late 1936 through September 1937, as recorded by the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo and the State Department. It details the promulgation of economic and national defense legislation from the 69th Diet, the contentious 70th session under Prime Minister Senjuro Hayashi culminating in the sudden dissolution of the House of Representatives in March 1937, and the general election of April 1937. It also documents the subsequent 71st and 72nd special sessions of the Diet under Prime Minister Fumimaro Konoe, focusing heavily on diplomatic relations, rising military tensions following the Marco Polo Bridge and Shanghai incidents, and Japan's escalating conflict with China.

subfiles.about: A summary report detailing Laws No. 16 through 45 enacted during the 69th special session of the Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: This report provides summaries of Japanese laws promulgated in May and June 1936 at the conclusion of the 69th Diet session. The legislation covers the establishment of the Northeastern Electric Power Development Company, amendments to the Railway Construction Law, state purchase of private railways, autonomous control of rice and cereals, encouragement and control of important industries and exports, and surveillance of persons convicted of dangerous thoughts. Additional measures regulate fertilizers, horse racing, automobile manufacturing, aviation, shipping services, import tariffs, and the establishment of the Taiwan Development Company.
subfiles.title: Summary of Legislation Enacted by the Sixty-Ninth Session of the Imperial Diet

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum and cross-reference sheet providing biographical information on former Foreign Minister Kenkichi Yoshizawa.
subfiles.summary: Biographic data on Kenkichi Yoshizawa, former Foreign Minister and Peers member, Institute of Pacific Relations attendee: career in Peking, Paris, the League, and as Inukai's son-in-law.
subfiles.title: Biographic Data Regarding Kenkichi Yoshizawa

subfiles.about: A despatch reporting the Imperial ordinance convoking the 70th session of the Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Tokyo reports the publication of an Imperial ordinance convoking the 70th session of the Imperial Diet for December 24, 1936, with the ceremonial opening scheduled for December 26. An archival charge slip from 1956 is appended noting the charging out of the despatch's enclosure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Diet to Convene December 24, 1936 (Despatch No. 2129)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet and excerpt from Despatch No. 2221 summarizing Diet-related developments in December 1936.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2221 extract (December 1936): the Diet System Commission proposes earlier convening and longer budget review; party opposition grows, including a Seiyukai free-speech resolution.
subfiles.title: The Diet: Summary of Developments During Month of December, 1936 (Despatch No. 2221)

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2271 (February 17, 1937): interpellations in the February 15-16 Diet sessions on the political situation.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Interpellations in February 15 and 16 Sessions of the Diet (Despatch No. 2271)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 2274 concerning an interpellation by Yukio Ozaki on February 17, 1937.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2274 (894.00/705): Yukio Ozaki's speech was heard with rapt attention and drew a restrained government reply.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Interpellation by Mr. Yukio Ozaki in the Japanese Diet (Despatch No. 2274)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note and telegram reporting Foreign Minister Naotake Sato's foreign policy address before the House of Peers.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains a document file note and the complete two-section text of Telegram No. 85 from Ambassador Grew analyzing Foreign Minister Naotake Sato's address of March 8, 1937. Sato reviewed relations with the Soviet Union, Great Britain, and China, notably advocating for dealing with China on a basis of equality and abandoning Japan's sense of superiority. Grew reports that financial and business circles welcomed Sato's moderate stance, although observers cautioned that the Kwantung Army might oppose his conciliatory policy.
subfiles.title: Statement on Japan's Foreign Relations by Minister for Foreign Affairs Sato in House of Peers (Telegram No. 85)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 2283 submitting a translation of Yukio Ozaki's Diet interpellation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2283 (894.00/712): Ozaki's February 17, 1937 interpellation, with an English translation from the stenographic report.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Diet Interpellation of Mr. Yukio Ozaki (Despatch No. 2283)

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2290 (894.00/713): Seigo Nakano's Diet interpellation, with background on Nakano.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Diet Interpellation of Mr. Seigo Nakano (Despatch No. 2290)

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2293 (894.00/715): important Diet interpellations of February 17-28, 1937.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Diet Interpellations from February 17 to 28, 1937 (Despatch No. 2293)

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting the dissolution of the House of Representatives by the Hayashi Cabinet and scheduling of elections.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the House dissolved March 30, 1937 with an election April 30; key measures failed. Dissolution stemmed from election law friction and the Cabinet's wish to avoid parties, favoring an army-led party.
subfiles.title: Dissolution of the Japanese Lower House and Setting of General Election (Telegram No. 101)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 2316 summarizing Diet proceedings in early March 1937.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2316 (894.00/719): Diet proceedings from March 1 to 16, 1937.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Diet Proceedings from March 1 to March 16, 1937 (Despatch No. 2316)

subfiles.about: A despatch with departmental memorandum and newspaper clipping reviewing Diet proceedings and the abrupt dissolution of the Lower House.
subfiles.summary: This subfile comprises a State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs analysis memorandum, Ambassador Grew's Despatch No. 2339, and a clipping from The Japan Advertiser. Grew details the events leading to the dissolution of the House of Representatives on March 31, 1937, after the budget was approved but political parties obstructed other Government bills over election law disputes. The despatch recounts interpellations on Soviet fisheries, trade relations, civil aviation, and the 'Imperial Way,' while the attached clipping lists 35 Government bills shelved as a result of the dissolution.
subfiles.title: Diet Proceedings from March 17 to March 31, 1937 (Despatch No. 2339)

subfiles.about: A despatch with departmental memorandum and newspaper clipping providing an analytical appraisal of the dissolution of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Accompanied by a Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum and a clipping from The Japan Times, this despatch analyzes Premier Senjuro Hayashi's motives for dissolving the Diet on March 31, 1937. Grew interprets the dissolution as an arbitrary disciplinary maneuver by military leaders against parliamentary parties, noting statements by Navy Minister Yonai and Premier Hayashi urging parties to reflect on their conduct. The report discusses the prospects of an Army-backed fascist party and provides voter registration figures for all prefectures in preparation for the April 30 general election.
subfiles.title: An Appraisal of the Diet Dissolution (Despatch No. 2350)

subfiles.about: A despatch with departmental memorandum, press clipping, and Foreign Minister speech text reporting on the 71st special session of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains a Division of Far Eastern Affairs briefing memo, Ambassador Grew's preliminary report on the 71st Diet session, a Japan Advertiser clipping, and the official Foreign Office English text of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's address. The special session convened on July 23, 1937, following the general election, and was completely dominated by the North China Incident. Grew analyzes major addresses by Premier Fumimaro Konoe, Foreign Minister Hirota, and Finance Minister Okinori Kaya, detailing supplementary military budgets totaling over 500 million yen and Japan's diplomatic stance toward China, Britain, the USSR, and the United States.
subfiles.title: Seventy-First Japanese Diet, Preliminary Report (Despatch No. 2525)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet and excerpt from Despatch No. 2524 reporting on the Diet's handling of the North China situation.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2524 extract: both Houses rapidly approved supplementary military budgets for China in late July 1937; Konoe, Hirota and Sugiyama say Japan seeks cooperation, not territory.
subfiles.title: The Diet: Proceedings of the Special Diet Session Regarding the North China Situation (Despatch No. 2524)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note and telegram transmitting the full text of Foreign Minister Hirota's address to the 72nd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains a document file note and the complete text of Telegram No. 340 conveying Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's September 5 address before the 72nd extraordinary session of the Diet. Hirota recounts the escalation of the conflict following the Lukouchiao Incident, the killing of Sublieutenant Oyama and Seaman Saito in Shanghai, and subsequent fighting in Central and North China. He outlines diplomatic exchanges with Britain, the United States, and France regarding proposed neutral zones, defending Japan's military actions as necessary to protect its nationals and force China to abandon its anti-Japanese policies.
subfiles.title: Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's Address on the China Affair at the 72nd Session of the Diet (Telegram No. 340)

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note and telegram transmitting Prime Minister Konoe's address opening the 72nd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 343: Konoe's 72nd Diet address says China answered Japan's restraint with contempt and mobilization, so Japan must deal a decisive blow while disclaiming hostility to the Chinese people.
subfiles.title: Prime Minister Konoe's Address on the Sino-Japanese Conflict at the 72nd Session of the Diet (Telegram No. 343)
